title: assign_devid_impl rollback logic: prev_safe_mode invariant is non-obvious
description:
What is unclear (for a contributor): crypto2dev_assign_devid_impl() saves prev_safe_mode before setting g_tls_safe_mode=1 and registering the device. On set_fn failure it uses prev_safe_mode != 0 to decide whether to unregister.

The intent is: 'only unregister the device if THIS call was the one that registered it.' The heuristic used is prev_safe_mode == 0, meaning no prior assign_devid call had run.

But this is not an exact test. A user who:
1. Calls wc_crypto2dev_init() (does NOT register the device)
2. Manually calls wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice()
3. Calls wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid(ctx) and set_fn fails

...would have assign_devid_impl call UnRegisterDevice (because prev_safe_mode == 0), removing the registration from step 2 as a side effect. This is documented in the header ('The TLS CTX/SSL continues to use WOLF_CRYPTO2DEV_DEVID') but the code comment at the rollback site only says 'prev_safe_mode != 0 means a prior assign_devid call already registered it' — which is the NORMAL case, not the documented edge case.

What would make it clear: A comment at the rollback: 'Note: if the caller registered the device manually before calling assign_devid, that registration is lost here. This edge case is documented in wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid() header.'

Or: track registration separately from safe-mode (an int g_devid_registered that assign_devid_impl sets on first register).
